question: What is the primary characteristic of structural cardiac disorders?
explanation: Structural cardiac disorders involve physical defects in the heart's valves, walls, or chambers that physically impair normal blood flow. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is rheumatic heart disease particularly significant in regions like Nigeria?

options.A: It is a leading acquired structural disorder among younger populations
options.B: It is exclusively caused by sudden genetic mutations at birth
options.C: It responds immediately to standard over-the-counter antimalarial therapy
options.D: It affects only the electrical conduction pathways without touching valves

explanation: Post-streptococcal rheumatic fever frequently damages heart valves early in life, making it a major clinical concern in developing healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h1)

question: What compensatory myocardial change typically occurs in response to chronic pressure overload?
explanation: To push blood against increased resistance, the heart muscle thickens over time, a process known as hypertrophy. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h2)

question: How does chronic left-sided heart valve failure ultimately cause pulmonary congestion?

options.A: By backing up blood flow into the pulmonary circulation
options.B: By relaxing the smooth muscle of the lower extremities
options.C: By decreasing overall fluid intake in the body
options.D: By opening a secondary shunt in the right atrium

explanation: When the left side cannot pump effectively, blood dams up behind it into the lungs, increasing pulmonary capillary pressure and causing fluid accumulation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the functional definition of valvular stenosis?

options.A: Complete calcification of the entire pericardial sac
options.B: Stretching of chordae tendineae into the ventricle
options.C: Narrowing of the valve orifice impeding forward flow
options.D: Incomplete closure allowing blood to leak backward

explanation: Stenosis refers to a narrowed opening that restricts the forward movement of blood through the heart valve. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h3)

question: A patient diagnosed with mitral regurgitation will primarily experience which hemodynamic abnormality?

options.A: Pressure overload in the aorta due to restricted outflow
options.B: Volume overload in the left atrium due to backward leakage
options.C: Complete cessation of coronary artery perfusion
options.D: Immediate closure failure of the tricuspid valve

explanation: Regurgitation causes blood to slip backward through a faulty valve during systole, overloading the chamber immediately behind it with excess volume. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which anomaly is considered the most common congenital heart defect?
explanation: VSDs represent the single most frequent congenital cardiac malformation diagnosed in pediatric populations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h4)

question: An infant with Tetralogy of Fallot suddenly experiences a hypercyanotic spell (tet spell) while crying. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Place the infant in a knee-chest position
options.B: Administer a large bolus of oral glucose solution
options.C: Position the infant flat on their back with legs extended
options.D: Encourage vigorous crying to expand lung capacity

explanation: The knee-chest position increases systemic vascular resistance, decreasing right-to-left shunting and improving pulmonary blood flow during a hypercyanotic spell. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which physical finding is classically associated with turbulent blood flow across a damaged heart valve?
explanation: Turbulence created by blood passing through stenotic or leaky valves produces audible vibrations known as heart murmurs. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a primary clinical indicator of structural heart disease in an infant during feeding?

options.A: Immediate rejection of all liquid formulas
options.B: Rapid weight gain exceeding standard growth curves
options.C: Sleeping uninterrupted through all feeding times

explanation: Feeding requires significant energy for an infant; heart failure from structural defects makes feeding exhausting, leading to sweating and poor weight gain. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is considered the gold standard non-invasive diagnostic tool for visualizing valve structure and function?
explanation: Echocardiography provides real-time visual and Doppler data regarding heart valve morphology and hemodynamic function without radiation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is cardiac catheterization performed in patients with complex structural heart disorders?

options.A: To permanently cure underlying congenital septal openings without surgery
options.B: To replace routine daily nursing physical assessments
options.C: To eliminate the need for any subsequent pharmacological therapy
options.D: To measure precise intracardiac pressures and visualize anatomy directly

explanation: Catheterization allows clinicians to map pressures within heart chambers and map structural anomalies using contrast dye before corrective interventions. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary therapeutic goal of administering diuretics in structural heart disease?

options.C: Reducing fluid volume overload and preload

explanation: Diuretics promote urinary excretion of excess sodium and water, relieving fluid congestion and lowering venous return to the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why are beta-blockers frequently prescribed for patients experiencing symptomatic valvular stenosis?

options.A: To stimulate rapid contractions of the failing myocardium
options.B: To slow the heart rate and prolong diastolic filling time
options.C: To cause immediate dilation of stenotic valve orifices
options.D: To dissolve existing thrombi inside the left atrium

explanation: A slower heart rate gives more time for blood to flow across a narrowed valve during diastole, improving ventricular filling. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is a major clinical drawback associated with the insertion of mechanical heart valves?

options.B: Complete inability to handle normal blood pressures
options.C: Rapid structural degradation within two years

explanation: Mechanical components carry a high risk of blood clot formation, necessitating continuous lifelong anticoagulant management. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h8)

question: What differentiates bioprosthetic heart valves from mechanical valves?

options.A: Mechanical valves are made entirely from biological human tissue
options.B: Bioprosthetic valves are tissue-derived and have a lower clotting risk but wear out faster
options.C: Bioprosthetic valves last forever without any need for future revision
options.D: Mechanical valves require no blood thinners under any circumstances

explanation: Tissue valves avoid the rigid requirement for lifelong anticoagulation but naturally degenerate over a period of years. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h8)

question: What is a primary rationale for administering prophylactic antibiotics before dental procedures in patients with prosthetic heart valves?
explanation: Bacteria released during dental work can seed onto abnormal heart valves or artificial material, causing a dangerous infection known as endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h9)

question: Which nursing intervention is essential during the early recovery phase following cardiac surgery to prevent pulmonary complications?

options.A: Encouraging deep breathing and incentive spirometry
options.B: Restricting all fluid intake to zero drops per hour
options.C: Keeping the patient completely immobilized in bed for a week
options.D: Avoiding pain medications to ensure the patient remains alert

explanation: Deep breathing and spirometry expand alveoli, preventing atelectasis and clearing pulmonary secretions after general anesthesia and sternotomy. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h9)
